answer: Split the question in two, because the two halves get different answers. (1) The disposal-review decision itself, once a records officer has actually made it, is a retrospective fact -- an act that took place at a given time, carried out by someone, resulting in an assigned disposition. That is squarely CRM's business: model it as an E13 Attribute Assignment (carried out by the records officer, P14) that assigns a disposition type (destroy / retain permanently, an E55 Type) to the file (E31 Document) via P141 assigned / P177 assigned property of type, with the reason -- statutory requirement vs. curator's judgement of historical importance -- captured through P17 was motivated by, pointing either to the statutory instrument or to a documented curatorial rationale. (2) The retention schedule and the 'next review date' are a different matter: they describe a future, not-yet-happened event governed by a standing administrative rule, and CIDOC CRM has twice, on the record, declined to bring that inside its core scope. Christian-Emil Ore stated the model's orientation plainly in the 'Retrospective and Planned Events' thread: CRM describes what has happened or is believed to have happened, not what is planned (t0608). When the SIG built an actual model for plans, it explicitly kept it out of CRMbase: Issue 166 records that dealing with future instances of E4 'will be subject of extensions of the CRM, and not part of the scope of CRM', and Issue 333 ('Model for Plans') closed by placing Activity Plan and Event Specification classes in the CRMsoc extension, not in CRMbase. The CRM's own introduction likewise frames the whole model as support for 'analytic discourse about what has happened in the past' (crm732#s0061) -- a next-review-date is the opposite of that. This lines up with the wider archives-vs-CRM boundary the SIG has drawn before: Martin Doerr described the archival institution's distinguishing feature as a 'mandate to safeguard records of another institution about their actions' (t1306) -- exactly the rule-governed, forward-scheduling workflow (retention schedules, review triggers) that keeps getting proposed as its own CRM-compatible model (records-and-archives-management, comparable to FRBRoo, t0603) rather than absorbed into CRMbase. So: do not model the retention schedule or the next review date as part of the file's documented history in core CIDOC CRM -- that belongs to the records-management/workflow system (or, if you insist on CRM vocabulary, to the CRMsoc plans extension, which is a different module for a reason). The disposal decision, once taken, can and should be captured in CRMbase terms as an E13 Attribute Assignment on the E31 Document.

rejected_alternatives.why_not: Its scope note (search.py concept E30) covers legal privileges such as copyright and ownership, not statutory duties to retain or destroy records -- 'statutory requirement' as a reason for keeping a file is not a Right.

rejected_alternatives.option: Modelling the retention schedule / next review date as an E4 Period or E5 Event in CRMbase
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Issue 166's outcome states that dealing with future instances of E4 'will be subject of extensions of the CRM, and not part of the scope of CRM' -- the SIG considered and rejected treating future/planned temporal entities as core CRM material.

This is where the SIG actually put plan/future-event modelling (Issue 333), but it is a separate extension module, not CRMbase -- confirms the retention schedule is not part of the base 'documented history' the case asks about.
